coupling: The first RAR5 change permits all 256 owner-name bytes and allocates a 257-byte buffer for the terminating NUL. The later RAR5 cleanup shrinks that buffer to 256 bytes while retaining the earlier 256-byte copy limit. Neither changed commit is unsafe in isolation: the first has space for the terminator, and the later change paired with the original 255-byte limit has space for it. Together, an in-range 256-byte EX_UOWNER name writes its NUL one byte beyond the stack buffer. A fix must reconcile the owner-name length limit with its storage size across the two commits; reviewing only the later buffer declaration or only the earlier limit obscures that shared invariant.
